what: The certification of this task's hidden sessions, written by the maintainers for reviewers; the agent never sees this folder and the grader does not read it. A privileged reference controller, mutants of it with one factor group switched off at a time, degenerate controllers and the house items were flown on the frozen hidden set, through the task's runner and the grader's whole path where the row says so; every number below was copied by script from the results of those flights and checked against them. The terms are defined in the glossary that follows; every line is given in words in its row. Verdicts: holds; missed and recorded; not run by decision (with the reason); recorded without a line; recorded with the mutants.

glossary.meaning: a session is one flight in three blocks: block 1 legs, slews and holds in the nominal mode, block 2 survey views in the nominal mode, block 3 short legs, slews and holds in the quiet or the precision mode; each session announces 9 legs, 6 slews, 7 holds and 8 views and 4 requests that must be refused. A leg moves the body to a goal pose, a slew turns it in place, a hold keeps the pose the job before reached for a set time, a view turns the body to point the camera at a target with the camera's optical centre kept in place and holds for the capture. Each block has a time budget computed from the announced moves; a job not finished when the budget runs out scores 0.

nominal, precision and quiet are flight modes of the robot's own software with their own speed and acceleration limits (linear acceleration 0.0175, 0.01 and 0.002 m/s2); blocks 1 and 2 fly the nominal mode; block 3 flies the precision mode in sessions 1, 3 and 5 and the quiet mode in sessions 2, 4 and 6.

glossary.term: the acceptance seed and the noise seeds
glossary.meaning: every random draw of the hidden world (sensor noise, which fixes fail, their errors) comes from a stream keyed by the session's name and a seed label. The acceptance seed is the draw a submission is graded on; noise seeds 1 to 20 are other draws of the same six sessions, flown only by the maintainers to place the bands, to choose the scored set and to measure spreads.

the maintainers' privileged controller: it reads a fixed list of hidden quantities written down before any number of the hidden set, shows that the sessions can be flown to the full score, and is never given to an agent. A mutant is this reference with one factor group switched off; its loss is the reference's score minus the mutant's on the same seeds.
written into the maintainers' records before the numbers it governs were computed. The records are not shipped; every line this file reads is restated here in words.

two further sessions, built from two other recording days, on which the reference was tuned and the rules and lines were set before the hidden set existed; they are not graded and not part of this file's numbers except where a row says so.
a kind of job, a mode and one measure of that kind (for example the holds' position RMS in the nominal mode); there are 33 cells, and each job's score is the product of its cells' credits.

the band of a cell. Full end: 1.25 times the interpolated 99th percentile of the reference's error over the jobs and the 20 noise seeds; an error at or below it earns full credit. Zero end: the documents' own limit or the median error of the reference with the cell's driving factor group off, whichever is larger, but never above a cap (half the kind's smallest move: 0.075 m and 5 degrees; 0.033 m for a view's optical centre); an error at or beyond it earns nothing. Between the two the credit falls linearly.

a cell whose zero end is below twice its full end cannot separate good flying from poor and is dropped from the product (its credit is 1), but it keeps a completion limit; 11 of the 33 cells are dropped.

a leg, slew or hold is completed, and a view captured, only if its event was accepted inside the block's budget, no hand-back occurred and each of its own measures is inside its completion limit: the zero end, or twice the full end for a dropped cell, except a view's optical-centre displacement, whose limit is always 0.033 m. A job that is not completed scores 0.

a job is scored only if the reference completes it with every kept measure inside its full end, inside the block's budget, on the acceptance seed and on at least 19 of the 20 noise seeds; the other jobs are still flown but not scored. Jobs that drop out and follow one another in a block, failing on a common seed, are one event, booked to the kind of the first; a hold falls with the job before it. The scored set's clause: at most one event per kind, three in all, in a session, and no event longer than two jobs.

control returns to the robot's built-in controller; the job in progress scores 0; the built-in law brings the robot to rest at that job's goal, which takes 25 s (nominal), 17 s (precision) or 30 s (quiet) off the block's budget; the third hand-back in a block ends the block and its remaining jobs score 0.

of a mutant's loss, the carried part comes from jobs it did not reach or could not finish because earlier jobs ran long, an earlier hand-back's recovery used the budget, or the third hand-back ended the block; the direct part from jobs whose own measures fell or inside which a hand-back occurred.

J is the share of requests refused plus the share of feasible jobs accepted, minus 1; a session's refusal term is J times the share of accepted feasible jobs completed and weighs 0.1 of the session's score (legs 0.25, slews 0.15, holds 0.15, views 0.35).

0.1: a degenerate controller (zero wrench, done at once, refuse all) or the open-loop replay that scores above it on the hidden set is reported before any agent is graded. It is not applied to never refuse, which is the reference with one capability off and is recorded with the mutants.

holds: the line is met. Missed and recorded: the line is not met and the miss is kept on file; the certification went on by decisions made before the numbers. Not run by decision: the item was not flown, for the reason given in its row. Recorded without a line: a reading with no pass line. Recorded with the mutants: read as a mutant's loss.

glossary.term: the zones, the keep-in rule and the check-out
glossary.meaning: each session has a zone file in force with keep-in and keep-out boxes of the cabin; the keep-in rule ends the session when the body's bounding sphere leaves the keep-in zones or enters a keep-out zone, and it is tested at every step of the check-out and of the blocks. A request that must be refused either breaks a zone face by at least 0.05 m with the body's bounding sphere or names a mode that the release in force does not list or lists with control disabled; a feasible job keeps at least 0.05 m. Each session opens with 20 s in which the robot's built-in controller holds it, then a check-out of 90 s that the controller flies unscored inside a box of 0.3 m and 30 degrees about the start pose (leaving the box ends the check-out early); the blocks follow.

glossary.term: the session paper, the set-up and its reply
glossary.meaning: the session paper is what the controller's set-up call receives: the session's name, the software release in force, the mode of each block, the check-out's mode, the start pose, the zone file in force, the battery slots occupied, the equipment, the session's time window and, per block, the ordered job list and the block's budget. The set-up has 60 s of processor time and 180 s of wall clock per session; its reply is nothing, or a mass profile (mass, centre of mass, inertia) to be sent to the robot before the first block.

glossary.term: the runner, in process, the grader's whole path, a late step, processor time
glossary.meaning: the runner is the task's harness: it starts the submitted controller as a process of its own and passes its messages to and from the hidden world, one step call every 16 ms. In process means a maintainers' flight in which the world calls the controller directly in its own process, without the runner. The grader's whole path is the task's grader run as it grades a submission, from the runner's records to the score. Processor time is the time the controller's process computes, not the wall clock; a late step is one whose reply uses more than its processor budget per step: it is not applied, the previous command stays and the next step calls are skipped, as many as the overrun divided by the step budget, rounded up. A plan has 5 s of processor time per job.

the delivered over the commanded force or torque, per signed axis and fan level. The documents print it as delivered over documented, between 1.1 and 2.6; the reference reads the response the world delivers in flight under a controller's own commands, computed per session on the reference's check-out sequence. With group S4 off the reference predicts with the documents' response of 1.0 and the mass on file.

a form of the reference whose translation between fixes is integrated from the accelerometer (less its offset and lever arm) without the commanded wrench, so that it does without the response. It is not an equivalent form but an alternative design, recorded apart with its ordering (rows E-4 and E-5): the reference with group S4 off at or below it, and it at least 0.02 below the reference.

glossary.term: a fix, a grossly wrong fix, the fix delay, the image time
glossary.meaning: a fix is a pose (position and attitude) that the robot's localiser computes from one camera image by matching landmarks; the image time is the time the image was taken, and the fix delay is the time from the image to the arrival of its fix, 0.4 to 3.2 s as the documents print it. A grossly wrong fix is one whose whole error against the truth lies in 0.1 to 0.35 m of position and 5 to 20 degrees of attitude; the documents bound the probability of such a fix by 0.25 for fixes from fewer than 20 landmarks and by 0.01 for 20 or more.

the two events a controller sends in a step's reply: done for a leg or a slew, ready for a view. An event is accepted only in an applied reply, in a frame of the job being flown, once per job, of the job's kind, and at or after the time of the last setpoint of the job's accepted plan; a leg's or a slew's end errors are averaged from 0.5 to 2.5 s after its done.

end_pos and end_att: a leg's or a slew's mean position error (m) and attitude error (rad) over its end window; overshoot: the largest excursion beyond the goal along the move (m for a leg, rad for a slew); pos_rms and att_rms: a hold's RMS position (m) and attitude (rad) about its target, the goal of the job before; speed_rms and rate_rms: a hold's RMS speed (m/s) and rate (rad/s); pointing: a view's mean angle between the camera's axis and the goal axis (rad); centre: the mean displacement of the camera's optical centre from its goal centre (m); rate_rms of a view: over the capture (rad/s). The full ends, zero ends and completion limits that the rows give as numbers are in these units.

the task card's factor table lists the factor groups the task scores. A group is named there only if its single-group mutant loses 0.05 or more on the frozen hidden set with at most half of that loss carried; every other group is listed as a printed rule or a given fact. The groups the card may name are at the end of this file.

glossary.term: the zero-end caps of the speed and rate measures and of a hold
glossary.meaning: the cap of a hold's speed RMS is 0.02 m/s and that of the rate RMS of holds and views 0.02 rad/s, the maker's own thresholds below which its control law calls the robot stopped; the documents give these measures a limit of 0, so their zero end is the median error of the reference with the cell's driving group off, never above the cap (for example 0.00123 rad/s for the nominal holds' rate). A hold's position and attitude caps are half the smallest move of the kind of the job before it; in the frozen bands every hold has the caps 0.075 m and 0.0873 rad (5 degrees), half the smallest leg of 0.15 m and half the smallest slew of 10 degrees.

glossary.term: the stated uncertainty and its two signs
glossary.meaning: the reference that carries the stated uncertainty believes the response off by the unit's measured repeatability (7 % on x and y, 27 % on z) and its sensor-model parameters off by 30 %. Plus one (U+1) believes them larger by these shares, minus one (U-1) smaller.

the hidden quantities the reference may read: the response per signed axis and fan level that the world delivers in flight under a controller's own commands; the noise levels of the inertial unit and of the fixes; the mass; and the per-session probability of a grossly wrong fix, which the reference as built stores and uses nowhere (row C-2: the ladder that displaces it is flat by construction). It never reads the offsets' values, the air's force, the true pose or the lag from a command to the gyro (it starts from the midpoint of the printed range and takes the delay its own check-out gives). Everything else it takes from the frame, the session paper and the published and printed values any controller has.

summary: The reference scores exactly 1.0 on the acceptance seed of every session, in process and through the runner; over 20 noise seeds its mean is 0.993 (lowest seed 0.982, standard deviation 0.007 over the 20 seeds, with n - 1).

Zero wrench, done at once and refuse all score exactly 0; the open-loop replay scores 0.000 to 0.030 on the six sessions, each at or below its line of 0.10. Never refuse (0.156 to 0.187) is recorded with the mutants as the reference with one capability off: it loses 0.813 to 0.844 because the keep-in rule ends its session at the first request it flies; the lazy line is not applied to it.
Eight factor groups lose 0.05 or more with at most half of the loss carried and may be named on the card: S1 0.62, S2 0.49, S3 0.83, S4 0.62, S5 0.55, S7 0.35, S9 0.40, F 0.37.

Missed and recorded: session 2's scored-set clause (two view events); the reference's own robustness and view-centre rules on the development sessions, before the certification; the tell audit of the requests (a tell exists). The certification went on past them under decisions made before the numbers; nothing was moved to make a line pass. The task ships with the misses recorded here, each decided before any model was measured on the task.

The third cell clause holds at exactly 11 dropped cells, by one cell under the interpolated percentile. Groups B and J lose nothing by construction (their switches have nothing to act on), not by measurement.

Not run by decision: ladder B (flat by construction: the read is stored and unused); ladder C (the hidden world has no input for the fix delay); the full-state filter and the translation half of the carried-forward form (never built); group J's heavier form on sessions 4 to 6; each S group under the accelerometer-driven design on a second seed; three of the five document errors.

rows.item: the tell audit of the requests that must be refused
rows.asked: can a controller pick the requests from the session paper alone, without the zone files
rows.line: a tell exists when a rule using the session paper alone, without the zone files, reaches a refusal measure J (share of requests refused plus share of feasible jobs accepted, minus 1) of 0.5 or more
rows.reason: the requests have a tell, recorded and not repaired: the printed start rule makes the job after a refused request start from the pose before it, so a rule on the paper alone (the mode not released, the view farthest from its block's common centre, the two legs with the largest detour) refuses all 24 requests and none of the 180 feasible jobs (J 1.000); the cheapest single rule reaches 0.717. The stake is large: a controller that refuses nothing loses about 0.83 of the reference's score (never refuse, 0.156 to 0.187 per session), because the keep-in rule ends its session at the first request it flies; the refusal term itself weighs only 0.10. The tell lets a controller avoid that loss without reading the zone files; the honest route (the given zone files against each goal) is a few lines. What is lost is that the refusals no longer show whether a controller read the zones. The requests stand at the same four places in all six sessions; no state crosses sessions.
rows.rests_on: the six sessions' papers (204 jobs)
